steps.say: Testing rules replace family history guesswork when TP53 hides behind varied tumours. Early onset plus a young affected relative opens the familial door. Sentinel childhood tumours test positive alone at any age. Very early breast cancer requires testing even without relatives.
steps.tx: Li Fraumeni syndrome (**LFS**, TP53 on 17p13.1, autosomal dominant) is diagnosed clinically using the revised **Chompret criteria** (genetic testing guidelines): a proband with a core LFS tumour under 46 plus a first or second degree relative with LFS tumour under 56, multiple primary LFS tumours with the first under 46, any age sentinel tumours (paediatric adrenocortical carcinoma, choroid plexus tumour, embryonal anaplastic rhabdomyosarcoma), or breast cancer under 31 years. Penetrance approaches 100 percent in females and 70 percent in males.

vis.alt: Component malignancies of Li Fraumeni syndrome.
vis.caption: Core LFS cancers across sarcoma, breast, brain and adrenal. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Radiation avoidance shapes every treatment choice once TP53 is known. Surgeons remove rather than irradiate breast tissue in carriers. Whole body MRI hunts second cancers yearly without adding radiation dose. Childhood ultrasounds check the gap that MRI leaves.
steps.tx: The LFS spectrum runs sarcomas, early HER2 positive breast cancer under 31 to 35, brain tumours led by pathognomonic paediatric choroid plexus carcinoma, hypodiploid leukaemia and paediatric adrenocortical carcinoma (50 to 80 percent germline TP53), plus melanoma. Ionising **radiation** must be avoided (mastectomy over lumpectomy plus radiotherapy) for extreme secondary sarcoma risk. The **Toronto protocol** (intensive MRI surveillance) runs annual whole body and brain MRI from birth, abdominal ultrasound every 3 to 4 months in children, breast MRI from 20 and colonoscopy from 25.

vis.alt: Intraventricular tumour invading parenchyma with hydrocephalus.
vis.caption: Sentinel choroid plexus tumour prompting TP53 testing. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A goitre family with odd childhood tumours requires DICER1 testing. Lung blastoma in a toddler plus thyroid disease in relatives forms the classic pair. Virilising ovarian tumours remain a hormonal clue in girls. Thyroid differentials decide between Cowden, FAP and MEN2 instead.
steps.tx: DICER1 syndrome (14q32.13 RNase III microRNA processing loss, autosomal dominant) presents familial multinodular goitre with follicular thyroid cancer, plus pathognomonic paediatric **pleuropulmonary blastoma** (lung tumour), cystic nephroma (kidney cyst tumour), virilising ovarian Sertoli Leydig tumours, botryoid cervical embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, pineoblastoma and pituitary blastoma. Cowden PTEN instead pairs follicular thyroid cancer with oral papillomas, FAP APC with cribriform morular papillary thyroid cancer, and MEN2 with medullary thyroid cancer.

vis.alt: Diverse childhood tumour spectrum in DICER1 syndrome.
vis.caption: DICER1 tumour spectrum from lung to ovary to thyroid. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Normal endoscopy fails this family, because submucosal cells escape every biopsy. Risk numbers support removing a healthy stomach in young adulthood. Timing follows the youngest affected relative minus five years. Breast surveillance runs in parallel for female carriers.
steps.tx: Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (**HDGC**, CDH1 E cadherin loss on 16q22, autosomal dominant truncating) carries 60 to 80 percent lifetime gastric risk with signet ring cells (mucus filled cells) hiding beneath normal mucosa, plus 40 to 55 percent invasive **lobular breast cancer** (single file cells) in females. Endoscopy cannot be trusted, so prophylactic total **gastrectomy** (preventive stomach removal) is advised between 18 and 40 years, or 5 years younger than the youngest affected relative, with annual breast MRI plus mammography for carriers.

vis.alt: Linitis plastica with signet ring cell adenocarcinoma.
vis.caption: Diffuse signet ring cancer mandating prophylactic gastrectomy. Credit: StewardMD.
